purpose: A standalone, source-bound, no-network browser exercise of fail-closed federation decisions and independent-view continuity when a coordinator, peer, or authority is missing.

terminology.CoConstellation: Discovery and relation map. A link is not availability.
terminology.CoFed: Candidate peering and compatibility interface; not a deployed CoFed service.
terminology.CivOS: Candidate operating UX that may project across cells/devices; no standalone deployed CivOS runtime verified.
terminology.CoStax: Candidate modular stack recipes; not proven synonymous with CoStacks.
terminology.CoStacks: Existing public, shadow/report-only automation repository. No global deployment controller.
terminology.CoOrbWare: Receiver-relative projection grammar, not a new source of truth.
terminology.CoEvo: Versioned proposals, independent checks, authorized promotion and recoverability.

scenarios.title: Normal browsing
scenarios.challenge: The catalogue and its example services are presumed reachable for this local simulation.
scenarios.decision: Allow inspection. Never interpret public discovery as permission.

scenarios.title: Coordinator unavailable
scenarios.challenge: The supposed global registry disappears. The loaded public page must remain useful without it.
scenarios.decision: Keep local read-only work; label remote freshness unknown. No hidden coordinator failover.

scenarios.title: A peer goes offline
scenarios.challenge: EntMent cannot be contacted. CoAcademy's own source-bound task need not vanish.
scenarios.decision: Keep unrelated read-only resources; offer source pointers without inventing a live peer.

scenarios.title: A capability is revoked
scenarios.challenge: A formerly authorized external writer loses permission.
scenarios.decision: Public reads may continue; refuse mutation, even if a cached claim says authorized.

scenarios.title: A manifest is stale
scenarios.challenge: Discovery metadata exceeds its validity window.
scenarios.decision: Never paint stale evidence green. Require revalidation before binding remote capabilities.

scenarios.title: Two sites claim release authority
scenarios.challenge: Two candidate writers target the same shared sitemap or domain.
scenarios.decision: Preserve both proposals, elect one authorized writer or hold. Never last-write-wins.

scenarios.title: Private data enters a public route
scenarios.challenge: A proposed manifest contains a credential, secret, or personal record.
scenarios.decision: Block public emission. Keep private evidence under a separate authorized custody boundary.

invariants.title: No compulsory central brain
invariants.rule: The already loaded page remains inspectable with the coordinator absent; no cold-boot independence claim.

invariants.title: Discovery is not trust
invariants.rule: No link or JSON entry is accepted as authority or receiver ACK.

invariants.title: Authority does not flow through links
invariants.rule: All scenarios forbid external writes; revocation and split-brain fail closed.

invariants.title: Data classes stay separated
invariants.rule: Public display excludes secrets and private identities; no synthetic customer data.

invariants.title: Only one elected actuator
invariants.rule: If there is no authorized sole writer, shared changes are held.

invariants.title: Freshness must be explicit
invariants.rule: Historic evidence is not current status and stale manifests cannot be green.

invariants.title: Human and machine parity
invariants.rule: This page's embedded fixture must match the machine-readable source contract.

task: Switch from normal to coordinator unavailable while offline; inspect the surviving local read-only view and the explicit authority HOLD.
